name: TechNova Fest
brief: Organise TechNova, a two-day college tech fest for about 1,500 students. It has a 24-hour hackathon, a robotics competition, three workshops and an evening concert. We need sponsors, venue and permissions, social media marketing, online registrations, stage, sound and lighting, food stalls, volunteers and security, and post-event accounts. Organising team of about eleven students; the fest should happen before the end-semester break, about nine weeks out.

tasks.name: Define fest scope, dates, and team roles
Prepare preliminary budget and financial plan
Book stage, sound, and lighting equipment
Arrange food stalls and catering contracts
Prepare workshop materials and speaker confirmations
Finalize event schedule (hackathon, robotics, workshops, concert)
Run TechNova event (2‑day hackathon, competitions, workshops, concert)
Post‑event accounting, sponsor thank‑you, and final report

risks.title: Venue permission delay
risks.event: Final venue approval is received later than planned
risks.effect: Venue booking and equipment setup are pushed back, delaying logistics tasks
risks.response: Submit permit applications early, obtain provisional written approval, and maintain regular follow‑up with the admin office

risks.title: Sponsor funding shortfall
risks.cause: Key sponsors postpone payment until after contract signing
risks.event: Expected sponsor funds arrive late or are reduced
risks.effect: Insufficient cash to pay for sound, lighting and marketing materials
risks.response: Approach a broader sponsor base, secure at least two backup sponsors, and keep a contingency reserve in the budget

risks.title: Online registration platform outage
risks.cause: The chosen cloud hosting service experiences downtime during peak sign‑up period
risks.effect: Reduced participant count and extra manual processing effort
risks.response: Deploy the platform on a reputable provider with SLA guarantees and prepare a manual spreadsheet backup for emergency registrations

risks.title: Branding assets delayed
risks.cause: Designer workload conflicts with other campus projects
risks.event: Logo and theme files are delivered after the social‑media calendar is set
risks.effect: Marketing content must be re‑created, pushing back campaign launch
risks.response: Set an internal design deadline one week before the marketing calendar deadline and allocate a second designer as backup

risks.title: Volunteer drop‑out on event day
risks.cause: Several volunteers have exams scheduled during the fest dates
risks.event: A quarter of the recruited volunteers are unavailable for briefing and duties
risks.effect: Volunteer briefing and on‑site staffing take longer, risking gaps in event support
risks.response: Recruit 30 % more volunteers than needed and cross‑train them to cover critical roles

risks.title: AV equipment malfunction
risks.cause: Some lighting rigs have not been serviced in the past year
risks.event: Lights or speakers fail during the concert or hackathon sessions
risks.effect: Event schedule is interrupted and audience experience suffers
risks.response: Conduct full equipment tests 48 hours before the fest and keep spare bulbs, cables and a backup speaker set on site

risks.title: Scope creep – extra competition added
risks.cause: Student committee proposes an additional gaming tournament midway through planning
risks.event: New competition is added without budget or schedule adjustment
risks.effect: Additional resources are needed, pushing back the final report and increasing costs
risks.response: Lock the fest scope in the project charter and require senior‑team approval for any new activity

risks.title: Rain affecting food stalls
risks.cause: Unseasonal rain forecast for the second day of the fest
risks.event: Outdoor food vendor tents become unsafe and some stalls cannot operate
risks.effect: Catering options are reduced, leading to participant dissatisfaction and possible refunds
risks.response: Negotiate contracts that include indoor backup locations and insurance for weather‑related disruptions

risks.title: Negative social‑media backlash
risks.cause: A promotional post is misinterpreted as endorsing a controversial technology
risks.event: Followers post critical comments and share the content widely
risks.effect: Reputation damage reduces expected attendance and scares potential sponsors
risks.response: Implement a content review workflow, prepare a crisis communication plan, and issue a clarifying statement within 24 hours of any issue
